resources.title: Lecture 16: Projection matrices and least squares (18.06)
resources.about: Strang derives least squares as projecting b onto the column space of A, giving the normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb, and fits a line to data.
resources.use: When the normal equations or the projection picture of least squares are not clicking.

resources.title: Lecture 33: Left and right inverses; pseudoinverse (18.06)
resources.about: Strang on matrices with only a left inverse, only a right inverse or none, and the pseudoinverse as the fix, tied to the four fundamental subspaces.
resources.use: For the pseudo-inverse, and for why the minimum-norm solution lies in the row space.

resources.title: Lecture 6: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) (18.065)
resources.about: Strang on A = UΣVᵀ as rotation, stretch, rotation, with the eigenvectors of AᵀA and AAᵀ and σ² as the shared eigenvalues.
resources.use: When the singular value decomposition itself feels shaky.

resources.title: Lecture 7: Eckart-Young: The Closest Rank k Matrix to A (18.065)
resources.about: Strang states and discusses Eckart-Young: truncating the SVD at k terms gives the closest rank-k matrix, with the norm background.
resources.use: To see Eckart–Young stated and discussed: the truncated SVD is the closest rank-k matrix.

resources.title: Essence of linear algebra, Chapter 7: Inverse matrices, column space and null space
resources.about: Geometric account of Ax = v, when an inverse exists, column space, rank and null space, on the 3Blue1Brown site with the video and a text version.
resources.use: When column space, rank or null space need a picture, for example with dependent columns.

resources.title: Data-Driven Science & Engineering, Chapter 1: Singular Value Decomposition (video lectures)
resources.by: Steven L. Brunton and J. Nathan Kutz
resources.about: The book's site page for chapter 1, with a video per section: matrix approximation, Frobenius norm, optimal truncation, and 'Linear Systems, Least Squares & Regression'.
resources.use: For video walk-throughs of least squares through the SVD and of optimal truncation.

resources.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
resources.by: Deisenroth, Faisal and Ong (Cambridge University Press)
resources.about: Free-PDF book for ML practitioners; the chapters most relevant here are 3 (Analytic Geometry), 4 (Matrix Decompositions), 9 (Linear Regression) and 10 (PCA).
resources.use: For projections, least squares and matrix decompositions in machine-learning notation.

resources.title: What Is the Singular Value Decomposition?
resources.about: A short, precise note on the SVD, the Eckart-Young theorem (best rank-k approximation in the 2-norm and Frobenius norm) and the pseudoinverse.
resources.use: For the exact statement of the SVD and of Eckart–Young.

resources.title: What Is the Pseudoinverse of a Matrix?
resources.about: Short note on the pseudoinverse: it gives the minimum 2-norm least squares solution, and it is built from the SVD.
resources.use: For a compact statement that the pseudo-inverse gives the minimum-norm least squares solution.

resources.title: Moore–Penrose inverse (Wikipedia)
resources.about: Reference article: the four Penrose conditions, construction via the SVD, and applications including minimum-norm solutions.
resources.use: For the four Penrose conditions and the construction from the SVD.

resources.title: Low-rank approximation (Wikipedia)
resources.about: Reference article stating the Eckart–Young–Mirsky theorem and proving it separately for the spectral norm and the Frobenius norm.
resources.use: To compare a proof of Eckart–Young for the spectral norm with a published one.

resources.title: Ordinary least squares (Wikipedia)
resources.about: Reference article on OLS, with the normal equations (XᵀX)β = Xᵀy and the projection interpretation. It is written in statistics notation (X, β, y).
resources.use: As a cross-check in statistics notation on the projection picture of least squares.

resources.title: Numerical Linear Algebra (Trefethen and Bau), author's page
resources.by: Lloyd N. Trefethen and David Bau III (SIAM, 1997)
resources.about: Trefethen's page for the book: 40 short lectures, with the front matter and Lectures 1 to 5 as free downloads.
resources.use: For a rigorous treatment of the SVD, projectors and least squares; only the front matter and lectures 1 to 5 are free.

resources.title: EE263 lecture slides (Stanford)
resources.by: Stanford EE263 teaching staff (course by Stephen Boyd)
resources.about: Slides for least squares (Lecture 10), least-norm solutions (Lecture 12) and the SVD (Lecture 17), as plain and annotated PDFs.
resources.use: For slides on least squares, least-norm solutions and the SVD.
